source.title: Component and Dimension Sparsity in Transformer Refusal Mechanisms
source.authors: Vincent Siu; Glenn Grant-Richards; Vlad Pavlovich; Yi-Zhou Sun; D. Song; Chen-Guang Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices and references; it is not visibly garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study extracts harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions and applies directional orthogonalization, reporting harmful-response attack success rates on four new open-weight instruct models. It also decomposes that intervention into component and dimension subsets.
record.gate_note: The study reports the selected-layer sweep only in figures, so its per-layer values are not separately recorded. Direction and layer choices used to select the intervention are not results rows. The paper does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, jailbreak attacks that suppress the direction, or training against ablation.
record.test_reason: The study extracts harmful-minus-harmless DIM directions in four new instruct models and orthogonalizes them, reporting LlamaGuard-3 ASR on 512 held-out harmful prompts. It also measures MMLU, GSM8k and Pile perplexity after baking the projection into weights. This is a different method from the original: a single-layer, component-output orthogonalization over layers below l*, not the all-layer, all-position ablation. The paper's main aim is decomposing where the direction is assembled.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal steering with one DIM direction is reproduced by a sparse subset of upstream components (28-48%, retaining 88-101%), and within them by about 50% of residual dimensions, consistent with a privileged basis. They add that attention components supply the discriminative signal while MLPs are diffuse, and that the sparse mechanism costs less capability than dense ablation. They explicitly limit the claim to how one direction is assembled, not the full refusal subspace.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless DIM direction and orthogonalization, but chooses one peak-effect layer per model and analyzes component- and dimension-restricted interventions rather than testing the all-layer/all-position intervention or direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Selected intervention layer varies by model; the component sets and ASR depend somewhat on greedy-elimination thresholds and tie breaking. Reported sensitivity runs show threshold-related ASR changes and differing component membership; native-basis coordinate masking also performs much better than masking a randomly rotated direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonalizing r* in only 28-48% of upstream components retains 88-101% of the dense steering ASR. Complements mostly fail (1.6-34.6%). Masking about 50% of coordinates retains 85-98%; bottom-magnitude or rotated coordinates fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The single refusal direction is assembled by a sparse, identifiable subset of attention/MLP components and concentrates in a basis-aligned half of residual dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: The sparse-mechanism weight edit keeps capability within about 3 points everywhere, including Phi4-Mini, where the dense edit is costly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting direction removal to the writing components and high-magnitude coordinates reduces capability cost compared with dense ablation.

record.problems: ASR is judged by LlamaGuard 3; the main mechanism and dimension results report no uncertainty estimates. Capability checks cover MMLU 0-shot, GSM8k, and a limited Pile perplexity evaluation. Rotation results use N=5. Results support steering at a selected layer but do not establish the broader all-layer/all-position or harmless-prompt addition claims.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numerical rows were omitted. Per-layer sweep values in Appendix C and plots without numerical descriptions were not extracted as values; layer choice and other selection-only measurements are excluded.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. Ablation at all layers and positions (only a single layer l* or layers below it). No unsteered-model ASR or refusal rate is reported as a baseline. Capability checks cover only MMLU, GSM8k and Pile perplexity.
Refusal/ASR is not measured directly on the baked checkpoints; the authors rely on exact equivalence to the hooked condition. The edit covers only layers below l*.
Not tested; the authors explicitly restrict the analysis to one direction.
Not tested; directions are extracted per model.

missing.what: Absolute held-out ASR when all upstream components are orthogonalized (0.834 Gemma, 0.959 Phi, 0.949 Qwen, 0.936 Mistral). This is the main V1/V2 removal result and the hook-equivalent of the dense weight edit.
Peak single-point residual-stream orthogonalization ASR per layer, which is the Table 1 denominator; shown only in a figure.

record.verdict_notes: No unsteered-model ASR is reported, so removal is inferred from high post-ablation ASR on harmful prompts. The ASR judge is LlamaGuard 3. Table 1 and Table 5 use different denominators (single-point residual baseline vs all-component). The ethics statement frames the work as jailbreaking.

versions.untested_parts: No addition of the direction to harmless prompts; no ablation at every layer and position. Capability is evaluated on MMLU, GSM8k, and Pile, not all other abilities.

The paper says the projection interventions are baked into weights as exact reparameterizations and evaluates capability of the resulting checkpoints, but does not report a separate harmful-request refusal/ASR result for the baked checkpoints.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The paper explicitly limits its analysis to one direction and does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No distinct measure of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
Directions are extracted separately per model; no cross-language, base-to-instruct, or direction-transfer test.
No manipulation or comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages.

relation.reason: Reports its own removal ASR (Table 5) and capability after the weight edit (Table 2) on four models.

tranche.reason: Uses Arditi's DIM direction and orthogonalization. But the intervention site differs (component outputs of layers below one peak layer, not every layer), and so do the judge (LlamaGuard-3 ASR) and layer selection. Its own all-component ASR and capability results bear on V1, so this is T2 rather than T1 or T4.

source_check.notes: Layer l* was chosen by ASR on the full test set (Section 3.1), so the 'held-out' all-component ASR is not independent of the layer choice. The text reports no ASR for the unmodified model and no test of adding the direction. Outside the text: Gemma-2 normalises sublayer outputs before the residual add, which may break the exact baked/hook equivalence claimed for it.
